title: TC002-authentication api should handle user registration and login securely
description: Test the Authentication API for user registration and login flows using JWT and social login, ensuring secure token issuance and profile retrieval with proper validation and error handling.
code:
import requests
import uuid

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:3001/api"
TIMEOUT = 30

def test_authentication_api_registration_and_login():
    session = requests.Session()
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/json"
    }

    # Generate unique user data for registration
    unique_email = f"testuser_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com"
    password = "TestPassword123!"

    register_payload = {
        "email": unique_email,
        "password": password,
        "full_name": "Test User"
    }

    user_id = None
    token = None

    try:
        # 1. Register user
        r_register = session.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/auth/register",
            json=register_payload,
            headers=headers,
            timeout=TIMEOUT,
        )
        assert r_register.status_code == 201, f"Registration failed with status {r_register.status_code}"
        register_data = r_register.json()
        assert "user" in register_data and "id" in register_data["user"], "Registration response missing user id"
        assert "token" in register_data, "Registration response missing token"
        user_id = register_data["user"]["id"]
        token = register_data["token"]
        assert isinstance(token, str) and len(token) > 10, "Token is invalid"

        # 2. Login user with registered credentials
        login_payload = {
            "email": unique_email,
            "password": password
        }
        r_login = session.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/auth/login",
            json=login_payload,
            headers=headers,
            timeout=TIMEOUT,
        )
        assert r_login.status_code == 200, f"Login failed with status {r_login.status_code}"
        login_data = r_login.json()
        assert "token" in login_data, "Login response missing token"
        login_token = login_data["token"]
        assert isinstance(login_token, str) and len(login_token) > 10, "Login token is invalid"

        # 3. Use token to get user profile
        profile_headers = {
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {login_token}"
        }
        r_profile = session.get(
            f"{BASE_URL}/auth/profile",
            headers=profile_headers,
            timeout=TIMEOUT,
        )
        assert r_profile.status_code == 200, f"Fetching profile failed with status {r_profile.status_code}"
        profile_data = r_profile.json()
        assert "email" in profile_data, "Profile response missing email"
        assert profile_data["email"] == unique_email, "Profile email does not match registered email"

        # 4. Test login failure with wrong password
        wrong_login_payload = {
            "email": unique_email,
            "password": "WrongPassword!"
        }
        r_wrong_login = session.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/auth/login",
            json=wrong_login_payload,
            headers=headers,
            timeout=TIMEOUT,
        )
        assert r_wrong_login.status_code == 401 or r_wrong_login.status_code == 400, "Wrong password login did not fail as expected"

        # 5. Test social login endpoint (simulate Firebase login)
        # Assuming there is an endpoint /auth/social-login expecting provider and idToken
        social_login_payload = {
            "provider": "firebase",
            "idToken": "dummy-firebase-id-token"
        }
        r_social = session.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/auth/social-login",
            json=social_login_payload,
            headers=headers,
            timeout=TIMEOUT,
        )
        # Social login with dummy token expected to fail, so check error handling
        assert r_social.status_code in (400,401,403), "Social login with invalid token did not fail as expected"

    finally:
        # Cleanup: delete the created user if id available and admin token present
        if user_id:
            # Admin token from instructions for admin routes
            admin_token = "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VySWQiOiI2MjQ1MGY1My00ZjBmLTRjYTUtODZhYi1iNTVhODUyZmQ4MmYiLCJlbWFpbCI6ImFkbWluQGFsM2FtZXIuY29tIiwicm9sZSI6ImFkbWluIiwiaWF0IjoxNzY5ODEwNTk0LCJleHAiOjE3NzA0MTUzOTR9.5vI7sno3XTFNl1l82SWOlxmVD_5dBiUhu8cQrvir_gQ"
            try:
                delete_headers = {
                    "Authorization": f"Bearer {admin_token}"
                }
                resp_delete = session.delete(
                    f"{BASE_URL}/admin/users/{user_id}",
                    headers=delete_headers,
                    timeout=TIMEOUT
                )
                # Allow 200 or 204 as success for deletion
                assert resp_delete.status_code in (200, 204), f"User deletion failed with status {resp_delete.status_code}"
            except Exception:
                # Silently ignore errors on cleanup to not mask test results
                pass


test_authentication_api_registration_and_login()

title: TC003-orders api should create and update orders with correct calculations
description: Validate the Orders API for order creation, ensuring subtotal, shipping, and discounts are calculated correctly, and test order status updates including secure webhook callbacks with HMAC signature validation.
code:
import requests
import hmac
import hashlib
import json
import time

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:3001/api"
AUTH_TOKEN = "Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VySWQiOiI2MjQ1MGY1My00ZjBmLTRjYTUtODZhYi1iNTVhODUyZmQ4MmYiLCJlbWFpbCI6ImFkbWluQGFsM2FtZXIuY29tIiwicm9sZSI6ImFkbWluIiwiaWF0IjoxNzY5ODEwNTk0LCJleHAiOjE3NzA0MTUzOTR9.5vI7sno3XTFNl1l82SWOlxmVD_5dBiUhu8cQrvir_gQ"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": AUTH_TOKEN, "Content-Type": "application/json"}
TIMEOUT = 30

# Assumed secret key for HMAC signature (usually must be obtained securely/configured)
HMAC_SECRET = b"your_paymob_webhook_secret_key"

def test_orders_api_create_update_with_hmac_validation():
    order_id = None
    try:
        # Step 1: Create Order with sample products and discounts
        # We'll grab products from the products API to build a valid order payload

        # Get product list
        resp_products = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/products", headers=HEADERS, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert resp_products.status_code == 200, f"Failed to list products, status {resp_products.status_code}"
        data = resp_products.json()
        # Extract products list from response data
        products = None
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            # Try to locate a list in any value
            for value in data.values():
                if isinstance(value, list) and len(value) > 0:
                    products = value
                    break
            if not products:
                # fallback: if keys like 'products', 'data', or 'items' exist
                for key in ["products", "data", "items"]:
                    if key in data and isinstance(data[key], list):
                        products = data[key]
                        break
        elif isinstance(data, list):
            products = data
        assert products and isinstance(products, list) and len(products) > 0, "Products list empty or invalid"

        # Select first product and sample data to create order item
        product = products[0]
        product_id = product.get("id") or product.get("_id") or product.get("productId")
        assert product_id, "Product ID not found"

        unit_price = product.get("price") or product.get("cost") or 100  # fallback price if not found
        quantity = 2
        subtotal_expected = unit_price * quantity
        shipping_cost_expected = 20  # assume fixed or included in API calc
        discount_expected = 10       # assume sample discount

        order_payload = {
            "items": [
                {
                    "productId": product_id,
                    "quantity": quantity,
                    "unitPrice": unit_price
                }
            ],
            "discount": discount_expected,
            "shipping": shipping_cost_expected,
            "customer": {
                "name": "Test User",
                "email": "testuser@example.com",
                "phone": "+201234567890",
                "address": "123 Test St, Cairo, Egypt"
            },
            "paymentMethod": "cod",  # cash on delivery as example
            "notes": "Test order creation for TC003"
        }

        # Create order
        resp_create = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/orders", headers=HEADERS, json=order_payload, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert resp_create.status_code == 201, f"Order creation failed, status {resp_create.status_code}"
        order = resp_create.json()
        order_id = order.get("id") or order.get("_id") or order.get("orderId")
        assert order_id, "Created order ID missing"

        # Validate amounts calculation in response
        resp_subtotal = order.get("subtotal") or order.get("subTotal")
        resp_shipping = order.get("shipping") or order.get("shippingCost")
        resp_discount = order.get("discount") or 0
        resp_total = order.get("total") or 0

        # Assert subtotal roughly equals expected (float rounding may apply)
        assert abs(resp_subtotal - subtotal_expected) < 0.01, f"Subtotal mismatch: expected {subtotal_expected}, got {resp_subtotal}"
        # Assert shipping matches expected
        assert abs(resp_shipping - shipping_cost_expected) < 0.01, f"Shipping mismatch: expected {shipping_cost_expected}, got {resp_shipping}"
        # Assert discount matches expected
        assert abs(resp_discount - discount_expected) < 0.01, f"Discount mismatch: expected {discount_expected}, got {resp_discount}"
        # Assert total calculation: subtotal + shipping - discount = total
        expected_total = subtotal_expected + shipping_cost_expected - discount_expected
        assert abs(resp_total - expected_total) < 0.01, f"Total mismatch: expected {expected_total}, got {resp_total}"

        # Step 2: Update order status (e.g. from 'pending' to 'processing')
        update_payload = {"status": "processing"}
        resp_update = requests.put(f"{BASE_URL}/orders/{order_id}", headers=HEADERS, json=update_payload, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert resp_update.status_code == 200, f"Order update failed, status {resp_update.status_code}"
        updated_order = resp_update.json()
        assert updated_order.get("status") == "processing", f"Order status not updated correctly, got {updated_order.get('status')}"

        # Step 3: Simulate secure webhook callback from Paymob with HMAC signature validation
        # Webhook payload to update order status to 'paid'
        webhook_payload = {
            "orderId": order_id,
            "status": "paid",
            "payment": {
                "method": "card",
                "transactionId": "txn_123456789",
                "amount": resp_total,
                "currency": "EGP",
                "paidAt": int(time.time())
            }
        }
        webhook_payload_json = json.dumps(webhook_payload, separators=(',', ':'), sort_keys=True).encode()

        # Compute HMAC SHA256 signature using secret key over webhook payload JSON
        signature = hmac.new(HMAC_SECRET, webhook_payload_json, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()

        # Send webhook POST to the webhook endpoint with signature header
        webhook_headers = {
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
            "X-Paymob-Signature": signature
        }
        resp_webhook = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/orders/webhook", headers=webhook_headers, data=webhook_payload_json, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert resp_webhook.status_code == 200, f"Webhook callback failed, status {resp_webhook.status_code}"

        # Verify order status updated to 'paid'
        resp_get = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/orders/{order_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert resp_get.status_code == 200, f"Failed to fetch order post-webhook, status {resp_get.status_code}"
        order_after_webhook = resp_get.json()
        assert order_after_webhook.get("status") == "paid", f"Webhook status update failed, status is {order_after_webhook.get('status')}"

    finally:
        # Cleanup: Delete created order
        if order_id:
            try:
                resp_del = requests.delete(f"{BASE_URL}/orders/{order_id}", headers=HEADERS, timeout=TIMEOUT)
                # It's okay if delete fails, maybe order status disallows deletion
            except Exception:
                pass

test_orders_api_create_update_with_hmac_validation()
testError: Test execution timed out after 15 minutes
